title: LDN 1295: The Giraffe Nebula
explanation:
# The Giraffe Nebula

A cosmic cloud of dust and gas stretches across the constellation Cassiopeia, its silhouette so perfectly resembling a long-necked giraffe that astronomers named it LDN 1295—the Giraffe Nebula—after our brain's powerful habit of spotting familiar shapes in random patterns, a quirk called pareidolia. This dark nebula is essentially a vast, interstellar shadow, blocking the light from stars behind it, and has challenged astrophotographers since it was catalogued in 1962 by pioneering astronomer Beverly Lynds.
